title: I’m sorry

fn.en: Apologize and respond to an apology; write a message of apology.

gr: the language of apologizing and of accepting an apology

can.en: I can apologize properly, in writing and out loud, and accept an apology.

rc: should have and the third conditional

acts.say: Say each one aloud and hear which sounds like a real apology.

items.x: It was my fault, and I should have told you earlier.
I’m sorry if you were upset by it.

These things happen, to be fair.
It won’t happen again — I’ve changed how I do it.

sub.en: A real apology names the thing, takes the blame and says what changes.

items.q: You are apologizing to a friend, informally.
o: I’m really sorry about last night.
I’m really sorry for about last night.
I really sorry about last night.

items.q: You are taking the blame clearly.
o: It was my fault, not yours.

o: Don’t worry, these things happen.

Don’t worry, that things happen.

acts.title: To: a.zhaksybek@bmk.kz
parts: 1 · name it in the first line
4 · what you have already done about it
text: Subject: The Tuesday figures — my apology
I would like to apologize for the Tuesday report. It went out with last month’s figures in the second table, and you found it in front of the client rather than in front of me.
It was entirely my fault. I built the file from an old template and I did not check the second table before sending it.
I should have checked it, and I should have told you on Tuesday afternoon, when I first suspected something was wrong, rather than waiting for you to find it.
I have sent the client a corrected version this morning, with a short note explaining the error, and I have asked them to disregard the first one.
From now on the figures will be pulled straight from the system rather than copied by hand, so this particular mistake cannot happen again.
Apologies again for the position it put you in.

items.l: the subject line and first sentence
items.r: name the problem immediately, with no build-up
takes the blame and gives no excuse
says exactly what should have been done
reports what has already been fixed
says what changes so it cannot recur

items.q: Which five words open the message? (I would like to … for)
items.a: I would like to apologize for

items.q: Which four words take the blame? (It was entirely … )
Which two words introduce what was not done? (I should … )
Which three words open the sentence about the future?
Which one word is used instead of “sorry” at the end?

acts.genre: Register · a message or a conversation
acts.title: Written or said?
text: A written apology leaves a record. It names the error, takes the blame in one sentence, and says what has already been fixed.
A spoken apology is faster and warmer, and the other person can accept it there and then. It can be very short.

items.x: I would like to apologize for the Tuesday report.
Look, I’m really sorry about yesterday.
Please accept my apologies for any inconvenience.
From now on the figures will be pulled from the system.
Don’t worry about it — no harm done.

lines: I would like [to apologize|to apologize for to|apologize] for the delay.
I [should have|should of|should had] checked it before I sent it.
Please [accept my apologies|accept my apologize|accept my apologies of] for any inconvenience.
If I [had checked|would have checked|checked] the second table, none of this [would have happened|would happen|had happened].

items.why: should of is never correct; it only sounds like should have.
sorry about something, or sorry for doing something — not both together.

w: none of this would have happened
items.why: RECYCLED from Lesson 31: the if clause never takes would have.

write.q: Write a message of apology of about 130 words for something real — a missed deadline, a message sent in anger, a meeting you forgot. Follow the model: name it in the first line → take the blame with no excuse → say what you should have done → say what you have already fixed → say what changes.
write.model:
Subject: Thursday’s call — my apology

Dear Marat,

I would like to apologize for missing Thursday’s call with the Almaty team. Nine people waited for twenty minutes and then rearranged their afternoon.

It was entirely my fault. The invitation went into a calendar I no longer use, and I did not check it.

I should have confirmed the time on Wednesday, and I should have called you the moment I realized, rather than emailing an hour later.

I have spoken to everybody who was on the call, and the session has been rebooked for Monday at ten, which suits all of them.

From now on I am running one calendar rather than two, so this cannot happen again.

Apologies again for the inconvenience.

Best regards,
Tilek

speak.q: Now apologize out loud, and then take the other role. Apologize in three moves — name it, take the blame, say what changes — and then accept somebody else’s apology without making them feel worse.
speak.model: Marat, I’m really sorry about Thursday. It was my fault — the invitation went into a calendar I don’t use any more, and I didn’t check. I should have confirmed on Wednesday. I’ve rebooked it for Monday at ten and everybody can make it. It won’t happen again. … And when it’s the other way round: Honestly, don’t worry about it. These things happen. No harm done.
